example: In `src/lib.rs`, a method `run` in `impl Thing` has selector `impl[Thing]/fn[run]`; a method `run` in `impl Trait for Thing` has selector `impl[Thing/Trait]/fn[run]`; and a method `read` declared in `trait Read` has selector `trait[Read]/fn[read]`. {cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_selectors`
rationale:
The example has three scenarios, and two tests in `crates/habeas-sdk/src/outline/tests.rs` carry `{test}` references to it. Together they cover all three.

- **`rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry`** (lines 35–100) builds an outline for the path `src/lib.rs`, the same file the example names. Its source declares `struct Thing;`, `impl Thing { fn run() {} }`, `impl Trait for Thing { fn run() {} }` and `trait Trait { fn read(&self); ... }`.
  - It asserts that the outline contains `impl[Thing]/fn[run]`, `impl[Thing/Trait]/fn[run]` and `trait[Trait]/fn[read]`.
  - It also checks that each selector resolves back to a node carrying the same selector, using `outline.resolve(selector)`.
- **`selectors_name_syntactic_ancestry_and_duplicates`** (lines 662–706) repeats the same three assertions on a separate source with the path `lib.rs`.

The tests name the trait `Trait` where the example names it `Read`. The selector shape is the same, `trait[<Name>]/fn[<method>]`, so this does not change what is covered. The inherent-impl and trait-impl cases differ only by the `/Trait` suffix, and both are asserted. The tests also cover related edge cases: an impl on a non-path self type (`impl[%5Bu8;%204%5D]/fn[edge]`) and duplicate names (`fn[repeated]#1` and `#2`).

The test setup and assertions cover every scenario and expected outcome in the example, so I judge it satisfied.

The Rust outline profile under {cite}`requirements.references.outlines` MUST
identify items by segments describing their syntactic ancestry within the file,
such as `fn[run]`, `struct[Packet]`, and `mod[local]/fn[run]`, and MUST NOT
resolve Rust modules across files. Functions, methods, structs, enums, unions,
traits, impls, modules, macros, constants, statics, type aliases, and extern
blocks MUST be outline nodes. Impl segments MUST be named by their syntactic self
type and optional trait path, as `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]`. `use`
declarations and other items without a suitable name MUST be anonymous. Selector
